output.methodChoice: EDF-2 diagnostic with two catalogue items (X12, X5)
output.brief:
What is going on: the store 14 rise is probably not yet proven to be real loss. The Q1–Q3 figures are interim estimates from rotating cycle counts, and the back-test shows a typical error of about ±0.6 points per quarter. The 0.8-point rise sits right at that edge. In comparable store-years, about half of such rises were not confirmed by the year-end count. Store 14's own full-count history also swings (1.8% then 1.5%). Recorded shoplifting incidents jumped chain-wide when a new incident app launched in April, while chain shrink stayed flat, so the incident rise is partly a reporting change. The night-stocker tip was reviewed on CCTV and found unsubstantiated. Department mix did not shift. Self-checkout and footfall are plausible but unproven contributors.

How sure: moderately. The causes are not settled.

Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject the proposal to drop it. Hold off on a guard, personnel action, or self-checkout changes until the full count is compared with the interim figures. Doubling cycle counts is a low-cost option. Do not suspend the named employee.
